subject: MSA + Order Form: indemnity redlines and coordination
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara.park@brightgrid.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@brightgrid.com
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: indemnity requests

Hi Soojin / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here at BrightGrid ran the MSA + Order Form by our legal team and we attached our redlines (BrightGrid_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf). The two main items they flagged are: (1) indemnity for third-party IP claims tied to model outputs and (2) defense control for certain categories of claims (we're especially concerned about open-source dependency claims and alleged patent infringement tied to generated content).

Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept a mutual indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from our usage and propose guardrails around defense control? If not mutual, we need clarity on when BrightGrid would be responsible vs Redwood.

Would appreciate a short call this week with your legal lead. Our timeline: procurement needs signed docs by end of next month to hit our implementation window.

Attachments: BrightGrid_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf, 52KB)

Best,
Sara Park
General Counsel, BrightGrid Inc

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>

Sara —

Thanks for the redlines and flags. Looping in Kimberly from Legal so we can move quickly. High level notes from product/sales: we can be flexible on carveouts for AI-generated output if there are objective guardrails (examples, repeatable repro steps, request logs). We need to protect for third-party claims that arise from customer-provided content or BrightGrid custom prompts/flows.

Kimberly — can you review BrightGrid's redlines and propose a compromise path (defend vs reimburse split, any caps, and evidence/notice windows)? Also please call out any regulatory or data-flow concerns if we agree to mutual indemnity language.

Sara — are you available for a 30-min legal-to-legal call Tuesday or Wednesday (PST)? Ben will join for implementation questions.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@brightgrid.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: indemnity requests — proposed compromise

Sara / Soojin / Ben —

Thanks for the redlines. I reviewed BrightGrid_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf and put together a short compromise proposal (attached) that aims to preserve production risk controls for Redwood while addressing BrightGrid's procurement checklist. Key points: 

- Mutual narrow indemnity for verified third-party IP claims caused by the other's breach or by content that party provided. We propose the following limits: aggregate cap = higher of (contract value x 3) or $1M for customer-originated claims; cosmetic changes welcome but need floor to avoid disproportional exposure.
- Defense control: Redwood requests lead defense for claims arising from Redwood model internals or our training data; BrightGrid may lead for claims tied exclusively to BrightGrid-provided prompts or customer content. Where control is shared we propose a single lead counsel with right-to-approve settlements > $50k.
- AI-generated output: carveout for claims that allege infringement solely based on model-generated text unless Customer provides reproducible prompt + example output + request logs within a 30-day notice window.
- Evidence / notice window: 30 days to submit technical evidence; cooperation obligations to preserve logs and samples.
- OSS and third-party libraries: Redwood will maintain a list of dependencies and provide notice of high-risk components; indemnity excludes OSS claims where customer modified components in their environment.

I've attached RDW_proposal_indemnity_20260524.docx with redline-friendly language and a one-page decision table. Please review and share any absolute dealbreakers. If BrightGrid agrees in principle, we can formalize an MAP (mutual action plan) and run a short legal-to-legal call to close.

Attachments: RDW_proposal_indemnity_20260524.docx (docx, 18KB)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Park <sara.park@brightgrid.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example, soojin_lee@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: indemnity requests — proposed compromise

Kim / Soojin —

Appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed your proposal and are encouraged by the middle ground. A few follow-ups before procurement signs off: 

- Can Redwood tighten the settlement approval threshold to $25k for settlements that include ongoing obligations (e.g., injunctive relief or remedial engineering)?
- We need a specific data-retention/evidence handoff timeline that aligns with our SOC 2 processes — 30 days for notice + 7 days for initial evidence submission might be tight; propose 45 days total with a 14-day initial packet.
- For AI-generated output carveout: BrightGrid can agree to provide prompt + sample output + request log, but we need Redwood to commit to a remediation commitment if a legitimate infringement is demonstrated (timeline: remediation plan within 14 calendar days of verification).

If we can align on the three bullets above, procurement is comfortable moving forward. We're happy to take a short DocuSign path once legal agrees. Proposed timeline: finalize language this week, execution by next Thursday.
